title: Can a thermometer show less than zero?
description: Two thermometers show forty and fifteen degrees Celsius, and the scale is followed down past the zero mark. A level below zero is read with a minus sign, and the video shows what that sign tells about the temperature. Keeko's doubt that a thermometer stops at zero is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the thermometer scale carries on below zero, and a reading there is a negative number that is colder than the freezing point of water. Watch for students who think zero means no heat, so nothing can be lower.

source: Look at the two thermometers showing 40 °C and 15 °C. How co
video_script.why: The child sees that the thermometer scale does not end at zero and that a reading below zero is a negative number.
video_script.substitution: The book's own two thermometers at forty and fifteen degrees Celsius, with the scale followed below the zero mark.
video_script.anchor: the two thermometers of the book, at forty and fifteen degrees Celsius
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a thermometer stops at zero because zero means no heat at all. Zero degrees Celsius is only the freezing point of water, and the scale in the book has marks below it.
video_script.payoff_line: A thermometer can show a negative reading below zero.

final_answer.value: A negative reading, for example -4 °C, colder than 0 °C
final_answer.spoken: a negative reading, for example negative four degrees Celsius, which is colder than zero degrees Celsius

hold_back: A negative reading, for example -4 °C, colder than 0 °C
maths_rules: 0 °C is the freezing point of water
a level below the 0 mark is a negative reading; a level above it is positive
order on the scale from low to high: -4 < 0 < 15 < 40, and lower means colder
the book's scale has marks at ten degree steps, so below 0 come -10 and -20
video_script.design: Two thermometers side by side, then one tall scale that is followed down past zero. Amber below zero, teal above. The example reading of negative four sits just below the zero mark.
